newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Acting US Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky has warned Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer that the US will impose tough trade sanctions should the Australian Federal Government relax the rules restricting compact disc, software and book imports. Page 1.

The rise of the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras from obscurity to international fame has led to a boom in the off-season travelling trade as travel operators and tourist centres build tour packages to form a growing national party circuit and reap the benefits of the A$50 million that spins off from the festival each year. Page 3.

Due to the explosion in Internet traffic, Telstra will have to invest an additional A$200 million over the next three years in additional capacity in its Customer Access Network (CAN), domestic long-distance and international networks. Page 5.

Further evidence has surfaced that News Corp Ltd is increasingly reliant on its film division, as the 154 per cent leap in earnings - based almost entirely on the success of Independence Day - masks weaker-than-expected earnings elsewhere in the glbal media giant. Page 33.

Internal cost pressures and aggressive competition are propelling Ansett International towards a loss for 1996-97, leading the airline to withdraw from its bid for a share of the rights to Bangkok. Despite this, Ansett has maintained it will increase operations to the vital Japanese trade and continue its push into China later this year. Page 33.

Independent expert Grant Samuel & Associates has forecast a lower net result of A$42.5 million for the December year for takeover target Placer Pacific Ltd, based on unaudited managements accounts. Canada giant Placer Dome has offered one Placer Dome share for every 15 Placer Pacific shares in a scrip offer for its 75 per cent Australian-owned subsidiary, valuing the company at more than A$300 million. Page 39.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The release of stronger-than expected wage data damaged hopes for a further reduction in official interest rates, as bond prices suffered their biggest one-day decline in almost four months and the dollar spiked in reaction to the news. Page 21.

A formal announcement is expected from Foster's Brewing Group Ltd today naming former Philip Morris senior executive James King as the new executive vice-president and chief operating officer for Asia for the group. The appointment follows Keith Lambert' resignation late last year from the position of senior vice-president of strategy and development. Page 21.

News Corporation Ltd yesterday announced that net profit for the six months to December fell by 1.7 per cent to A$690 million, leaving investors cautious about whether the company will reach its goal of a 20 per cent lift in full-year earnings. An abnorml loss of $41 million, resulting from the sale of the HarperCollins education books division, contributed to the decline in net profit. Page 21.

Plans by Ansett International to begin flights to Bangkok have been scrapped as the company withdrew its application with the government air capacity regulator. The move coincided with the release of first-half results for Ansett's domestic and overseas operation, showing a worse than expected loss for the international arm of the company, although the domestic carrier recorded a small after-tax profit. Page 21.

West Australian Newspapers Holdings Ltd yesterday announced a 6.6 per cent slide in net profit for the December half to A$25.31 million compared with A$27.09 million in corresponding period of 1995. Operating profit also dipped by 4.1 per cent to $40.42 million, but the losses are fairly modest after a shortened trading period and bleak advertising conditions. Page 23.

The NSW Government yesterday approved a proposed gas pipeline from Wodonga to Wagga Wagga giving Bass Strait gas its first entry into the State. The pipeline will link existing systems in NSW and Vic, and will be built by East Australian Pipeline Ltd and the Vic Gas Transmission Corp. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Rupert Murdoch's forecast of a 20 per cent jump in News Corporation's 1996 earnings has come under pressure after the world media group suffered a 1.7 per cent fall in net profit to A$690 million in December. The result was led by a loss from its 50 per cent-wned Ansett Airlines and a poor performance from its US television division. Page 25.

The Colonial Group is poised to increase its business in Asia with the A$200 million buy-out of its joint-venture partner in region, Jardine Pacific Holdings. Jardine-CMG owns life businesses in Hong Kong, the Philippines and Singapore. It is believed the details of the deal will be released in Hong Kong next week. Page 25.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has warned the corporate community against returning to the sharp business practices of the 1980's. Speaking in the wake of the sentencing of former corporate hero Alan Bond, Costello said the Government would encourage its corporate watchdog, the Australian Securities Commission, to be vigilant of any signs of the 1980s business practices returning. Page 25.

Lloyd Williams's Hudson Conway has entered financial markets aiming to raise A$100 million as it hopes to lift its stake in Melbourne's Casino, Crown Ltd and win the bid to develop the Docklands site. It is believed Hudson Conway sought to raise the capital through unsecured notes with options attached. Page 27.

National Australia Bank is believed to be the front-runner over the Commonwealth Bank in the bid for Axiom Funds Management - formerly the NSW Government's State Super Corporation - in a bid which is expected to top A$150 million. Page 27.

According to Audit Bureau of Circulation figures for the six months to December 31 the Australian newspaper market is continuing one of its strongest periods of growth in recent history. Although there were circulation gains across-the-board for all titles, the highest gain was achieved by The Age which lifted sales by 7.3 per cent. Page 29.
THE AGE

Colonial Group is poised to double its business in Asia with a A$200 million buy-out of its joint-venture partner Jardine Pacific Holdings. Although Colonial's head of public affairs, Matthew Percival, refused to comment on the speculation, sources said the details of the purchase will be announced next week by the group's managing director, Peter Smedley. Page C1.

The ANZ Bank has unveiled a restructure of its investment division yesterday as its new head, John Sunderland, forecasting its profitability in Asia will double in the next three years. The investment banking division will move to an organisational structre based on product lines rather than its geographic base. Page C3.

Japanese authorities have approved discounts of up to 6 per cent on package tours to Australia. It is believed the discounts -yet to be announced by transport authorities in Tokyo - will take effect next month. The move has come at a time when Australia's stake in Japan's tourism market is falling. Page C3.

Ashton Mining has ended its long association with Helix Resources when it sold its 12.6 per cent stake in the Gawler Craton high-flier for A$26.56 million. The shares have gone to a single, unnamed-buyer although observers believe the buyer is likely to b a non-threatening institution. Page C3.

Strong results from Wattyl's new US businesses and sales from new paint products pushed the paint manufacturer's net profits up 16 per cent to A$12.3 million. Most of the gain in profit was due to the group's April 1996 purchase of Chicago-based Premier Catings. Page C3.

Tyre manufacturer, Bridgestone rolled in to a 4.3 per cent net profit rise to A$15.8 million, despite a fall in pre-abnormal operating profit, with sales also rising 1.6 per cent to A$437.8 million. The abnormal gain of A$4.987 million resulted from a reassessment of the useful life of Bridgestone's plant. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
